proposals.after: Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi crossed the river and invaded Fengyi; the Grand Progenitor led his army into Guan from Hongnong. Dao directed the left and right imperial guard, joined at Shayuan, fought Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi, and inflicted a great defeat.
proposals.reason: 齊神武 is Gao Huan's retrospective posthumous title, and 沙苑 is Shayuan, not Shaye.

proposals.before: When Gao Huan, Duke of Qi Shenwu, crossed the river and invaded Fengyi, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai led his army into Guan from Hongnong. Yuwen Dao directed the left and right imperial guard, joined at Shaye, fought Gao Huan, and inflicted a great defeat.
proposals.after: When Gao Huan crossed the Yellow River and invaded Fengyi, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai led his army into the passes from Hongnong. Yuwen Dao led the imperial guards to join him at Shayuan, where they fought Gao Huan and inflicted a crushing defeat.
proposals.reason: The existing English invents a dukedom, mistransliterates 沙苑, and leaves the military sequence awkward. The revision identifies the Yellow River, Hangu Pass region, and Battle of Shayuan clearly.

proposals.before: When Gao Huan, Duke of Qi Shenwu, attacked Shayuan, Xing was among the ranks; the army was defeated and he was taken captive, and by precedent was dispersed and assigned to various armies.

proposals.reason: The original invents a dukedom and obscures the change of subject and the treatment of the captive Yuwen Xing.
